rows.reason: Input 1: the story is a UI feature and the definition of done needs every requirement checked. Input 2: T5 covers an alias edit only; the project change has no UI coverage. Input 3: B-3 and B-5 matter. Input 4: observable and deterministic with an API read-back. The e2e-ui level is earned by the highest-risk user path of the story: an enabled dropdown plus the submit gate cannot be reached through the API, and the developer tests are component-level with mocks. One test with parameters, not one per assertion.

rows.what_we_verify: Records what happens when a user moves their user-scope integration into a project they do not administer; the expected outcome is not stated.
rows.defect_hypothesis: permission @ update_user_setting: project_name change with no target-project check
rows.reason: Observable, but no source says whether a user-scope move needs permission on the target (R-13 names project-scope integrations only). An unresolved oracle does not authorize an automated assertion, so the agent records the actual outcome with state evidence once and the owner judges it in the report.
rows.technique: error guessing on the permission boundary, outcome recorded
rows.risk_rationale: If a user can push an integration with credentials into any project, this is an access hole; if it is intended, nothing happens. The consequence is unknown, so it is not treated as low.

rows.test_level_rationale: Rung of P19: reachable by an API call, but the expected value is unsettled, so an agent records the outcome by hand rather than a test asserting a guess.
